concepts.title: Economic Activities and Definition of a Worker
concepts.definition: An economic activity encompasses all actions contributing to national product, and any individual engaged in such productive efforts—whether self-employed, hired, or temporarily absent due to illness—is classified as a worker.
concepts.key_idea: Every individual contributing directly or through assisting roles to the production of goods and services is part of the workforce.

solution_steps.explain: Check if the activity contributes to the generation of goods, services, or gross national product.
Individuals engaged in productive activities, including self-employed, unpaid family helpers, and those temporarily abstaining from duty, are designated as workers.

concepts.title: Worker-Population Ratio
concepts.definition: The worker-population ratio measures the proportion of a country's total population that actively participates in the production of goods and services.
concepts.key_idea: A higher worker-population ratio indicates greater engagement of the population in economic activities.
question_patterns: calculate the worker-population ratio
find the worker-population ratio given total workers and population

Explain worker-population ratio in your own words.

solution_steps.action: divide total workers by total population
solution_steps.explain: Ratio of economically active individuals to the total resident population
Multiply the ratio by 100 to obtain the worker-population ratio percentage

concepts.title: Estimation of Workforce from Worker-Population Ratio
concepts.definition: The total workforce in a given region or country can be calculated by applying the worker-population ratio to the aggregate population.
concepts.key_idea: Total number of employed persons equals the product of population and participation rate divided by 100.

concepts.title: Classification of Workers by Employment Status
concepts.definition: Workers are grouped into self-employed individuals who operate their own enterprise, regular salaried employees who receive periodic wages with job continuity, and casual wage labourers hired intermittently without job security.
concepts.key_idea: Employment status reflects the nature of contractual arrangement, level of security, and authority over production.

solution_steps.action: identify ownership of enterprise or contractual relation
solution_steps.explain: Determine whether the worker owns the business (self-employed), holds ongoing employment with regular pay (salaried), or is hired on day-to-day terms (casual).
Place into self-employed, regular salaried employee, or casual wage labourer based on terms of remuneration and attachment.

concepts.title: Sectoral Distribution of Workforce
concepts.definition: Workforce allocation across primary (agriculture, mining), secondary (manufacturing, construction, utilities), and tertiary (services, trade, transport) sectors reflects economic structural composition.
concepts.key_idea: Economic development traditionally drives structural shifts from primary agriculture to secondary manufacturing and tertiary service sectors.

concepts.title: Jobless Growth and Casualisation of Workforce
concepts.definition: Jobless growth is a macroeconomic state where GDP expands without generating proportional employment opportunities, whereas casualisation refers to the structural drift of labour toward temporary casual wage work.
concepts.key_idea: Output expansion through capital-intensive methods fails to absorb labour, pushing displaced workers into unprotected casual jobs.

concepts.title: Informalisation of the Workforce
concepts.definition: Formal sector units comprise public enterprises and private establishments with 10 or more hired workers providing social security, while informal units comprise all remaining small enterprises, self-employed, and casual laborers lacking social protection.
concepts.key_idea: The informal sector lacks labour legislation protections, social security benefits, and trade union representation.

concepts.title: Forms of Unemployment: Open, Disguised, and Seasonal
concepts.definition: Unemployment occurs when individuals willing and able to work at prevailing wages cannot find work; it manifests as open unemployment, disguised unemployment (marginal productivity of surplus labour is zero), or seasonal unemployment (lack of year-round agricultural work).
concepts.key_idea: Disguised unemployment conceals excess labour in farming where removing workers does not diminish total output.

solution_steps.explain: Determine if workers are visibly without work (open), working on family farms beyond actual labour requirements (disguised), or idle during off-season (seasonal).
Assign the appropriate category based on seasonal cycles or zero marginal productivity.

concepts.title: Government Direct and Indirect Employment Generation
concepts.definition: The government generates employment directly by hiring staff in public departments and state-owned enterprises, and indirectly through multiplier effects when increased public sector output stimulates demand in supplying and purchasing private industries.
concepts.key_idea: Public enterprise expansion and statutory schemes like MGNREGA provide both direct livelihood and stimulate indirect private sector employment.

solution_steps.explain: Public administration, state utilities, and public sector undertakings hire workers on government payroll.
Backward and forward industrial linkages cause private enterprises supplying inputs or processing outputs to expand their own hiring.
